t:
As used in this title—

    (a) 
The term “person” includes an individual, corporation, partnership, association, or any other organized group of persons, or a legal successor or representative of any of the foregoing.
 
    (b) 
The term “housing accommodations” means any building, structure, or part thereof, or land appurtenant thereto, or any other real or personal property rented or offered for rent for living or dwelling purposes (including houses, apartments, rooming- or boarding-house accommodations, and other properties used for living or dwelling purposes) together with all privileges, services, furnishings, furniture, and facilities connected with the use or occupancy of such property.
 
    (c) 
The term “controlled housing accommodations” means housing accommodations in any defense-rental area, except that it does not include—

        (1) 
those housing accommodations, in any establishment which is commonly known as a hotel in the community in which it is located, which are occupied by persons who are provided customary hotel services such as maid service, furnishing and laundering of linen, telephone and secretarial or desk service, use and upkeep of furniture and fixtures, and bellboy service; or
 
        (2) 
any motor court, or any part thereof; or any tourist home serving transient guests exclusively, or any part thereof; or
 
        (3) 
any housing accommodations (A) the construction of which was completed on or after February 1, 1947, or which are additional housing accommodations created by conversion on or after February 1, 1947, except that contracts for the rental of housing accommodations to veterans of World War II and their immediate families, the construction of which was assisted by allocations or priorities under Public Law 388, Seventy-ninth Congress, approved May 22, 1946, shall remain in full force and effect, or (B) which at no time during the period February 1, 1945, to January 31, 1947, both dates inclusive, were rented (other than to members of the immediate family of the occupant) as housing accommodations.
  
    (d) 
The term “defense-rental area” means any part of any area designated under the provisions of the Emergency Price Control Act of 1942, as amended, prior to March 1, 1947, as an area where defense activities have resulted or threaten to result in an increase in the rents for housing accommodations inconsistent with the purposes of such Act, in which maximum rents were being regulated under such Act on March 1, 1947.
 
    (e) 
The term “rent” means the consideration demanded or received in connection with the use or occupancy or the transfer of a lease of any housing accommodations.

fable.w: This section only defines terms ("person", "housing accommodations", "controlled housing accommodations", "defense-rental area", "rent") for a rent-control title. The tempting reading is that the definition of "person" or the reference to areas "designated" under the Emergency Price Control Act implies outside involvement, but these are definitional and refer to past designations. Nothing here provides for consultation, hearings, comment, rulemaking, an advisory body, or a right for an outside party to sue over a federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of statutory definitions for terms such as 'person,' 'housing accommodations,' 'controlled housing accommodations,' 'defense-rental area,' and 'rent.' It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, public comment, or advisory input from outside parties. It merely defines the scope of the statute's application.
qwen_block.s: As used in this title— (a) The term “person” includes an individual, corporation, partnership, association, or any other organized group of persons, or a legal successor or representative of any of the foregoing. (b) The term “housing accommodations” means any building, structure, or part thereof, or land appurtenant thereto, or any other real or personal property rented or offered for rent for living or dwelling purposes...

opus.w: This is a definitions section that defines 'person,' 'housing accommodations,' 'controlled housing accommodations,' 'defense-rental area' and 'rent.' It sets up no process for people outside the federal government to take part in a federal decision. The reference to areas 'designated under' the Emergency Price Control Act describes designations already made in the past. It does not create any future consultation or public input, so it is not participation.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The definition of "defense-rental area" points to areas "designated under the provisions of the Emergency Price Control Act of 1942." That could look like a reference to an administrative decision process. It fails because the designation already happened (before March 1, 1947), and this section creates no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue. It only defines terms.

qwen_chat.w: This section consists entirely of definitions for terms such as 'person,' 'housing accommodations,' and 'rent.' It does not describe any process of consultation, coordination, public comment, or advisory input from outside parties before a federal decision is made. Defining who is subject to the law is not the same as requiring their participation in the decision-making process.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that defining "person" to include corporations and associations implies that these outside entities are participants in the regulatory scheme. However, definitions alone do not constitute a process of consultation, coordination, or public input. They merely establish the scope of who is subject to the law. There is no mechanism described here for these entities to advise, comment on, or influence a federal decision before it is made.
